text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hassan inaugurates Al Wahda dam, saying "it will provide 250,000 jobs and bring irrigated land to one million hectares (2.5 million acres)".
- Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro says "Morocco is a reference for all those who respect democracy ideals."
- King Hassan and Italian President Scalfaro launch work on building a 130 km (80 miles) double railway line to link Kenitra, 40 km (25 miles) from Rabat, to central city of Meknes.
- King Hassan tells participants at Arab nationalist conference of "need to close ranks and clear atmosphere between Arab countries".
- Cabinet meeting considers additional clause to draft electoral law allowing further revision of electoral lists.
- French-Italian group SGS Thomson plans to invest $360 million in Morocco for extension over five years of electronics factory in Casablanca.
- Morocco and India signed a $230 million accord to set up a joint venture to produce phosphate by-products.
- Cut in interest rates on loans for small and medium-sized firms paves way for economic relaunch.
- Small and medium-sized firms more worried about conditions to obtain loans than cuts in interest rates.
